reader.requirement: At --std 85 every file the implementation supports must fall into one of GR2's three categories (non-reel/unit, sequential single-reel/unit, sequential multi-reel/unit), and each CLOSE form must then have that category's Table 1 effect; for the mass-storage files this implementation supports (non-reel/unit), CLOSE and WITH LOCK close (LOCK then refuses a reopen with 38), WITH NO REWIND closes with 07 (C,H), and REEL/UNIT [FOR REMOVAL] leaves the file open with its position unchanged and status 07 (F).

edition-consulted.switches: DialectBehavior.CloseWithLockLocksFileConnector: at 85 the PHYSICAL FILE is locked (symbol E 'The file is locked and cannot be opened again during this execution of this run unit'), so another file-name on the same file also gets 38; 2002+ locks the connector
WITH LOCK admitted at 85, refused at 2023

reader.edition-search: Table14.Cell, PhysicalFileCategory and the Category overrides read no edition (grepped Edition|DialectBehavior in CloseTable14.cs, SequentialConnector.cs#Category, FileRegistry.cs#CloseCell); the 1985 Table 1 non-reel column (C; C,E; C,H; F; F) coincides with 2023 Table 14's non-unit column plus the LOCK layer.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: CLOSE WITH LOCK locks the physical file at 85 (any file-name) and only the connector from 2002; WITH LOCK is refused at 2023
reader.witnesses-cover: part: pb141 covers REEL, UNIT FOR REMOVAL, NO REWIND on an output sequential file; not input or I-O mode, the FPI after CLOSE REEL on input, WITH LOCK, or the relative/indexed files and their refusal of the sequential-only phrases

reader.notes: The categories are an enum on the connector (every sequential file NonUnit) and the CLOSE dispatch executes the Table cell; categories (b)/(c) exist but no supported medium is placed in them, which GR2 permits (the classification applies to the media an implementation has). The two refusals at 85 cite §2023:14.9.6.3 SR1 instead of a 1985 rule: a citation nit, outside this rule.

refuter.evidence: Probe E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/coderead-1985/out/refute-1985-024/r5_close_gr2.cob (--std 85, run dir r5_close_gr2-002) took the open modes the reader's p5 did not, on the non-reel/unit category: EXTEND (a 1985 mode) 'EXT-OPEN=00 EXT-REEL=07 EXT-WRITE=00 EXT-REMOVAL=07 EXT-WRITE2=00 EXT-NOREW=07' (F keeps the file open, C,H closes with 07); I-O 'IO-READ=00 R=AAAA IO-REEL=07 IO-READ2=00 R=BBBB' (F leaves the file position indicator unchanged), 'IO-REWRITE=00 IO-NOREW=07'; reading back gives AAAA, bbbb, CCCC then 10 (the extended records were written and the rewrite applied); an INPUT CLOSE WITH LOCK then 'REOPEN-LOCKED=38' while another physical file opens 00 (E locks that file only). Two draft errors were 1985 refusals of my own source (COBOL6826, §1985:VII.4.4.3 SR2: READ with no AT END and no USE), correct at this edition. Every result is the non-reel/unit column of Table 1 (C; C,E; C,H; F; F) with status 07 per VII.1.3.5 item 1d.
